newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Central Bank CD auction yields fall.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Central Bank CD auction yields fall.

text.p: The Central Bank of Jordan on Thursday said yields dropped at its latest auction of 80 million dinars ($113 million) worth of bi-monthly certificates of deposit (CDs).

The average yield for three-month paper announced for the competitive auction which closed on Wednesday fell to 8.39 percent from 8.52 percent at the last auction. Six-month paper also dropped to 8.46 percent from 8.75 percent in the last auction.
The yield offers for three-month paper which were accepted were in a 8.50 percent-8.00 percent range compared to a 8.70 percent-8.50 percent range in the last auction.
Six-month CDs yield offers which were accepted by the bank were in a 8.55 percent-8.25 percent range against a 8.8125 percent-8.625 percent range in the previous auction.
Total bids received were 168.6 million dinars of which 65 million dinars were for three-month paper and the remaining 103.6 million dinars bids offered for six-month paper.
The three-month paper was covered 1.63 times while the six-month paper was covered 2.59 times.
The Central Bank sold 40 million dinars worth of three-month CDs and a similar amount of six-month CDs.

The Central Bank introduced last month for the first time a market-dictated CD auction system and began announcing yields in line with supply and demand as part of moves to adopt a move flexible interest rates structure.
Previously interest rates on three-month paper had been fixed for over a year at 9.25 percent and for six-month paper at 9.50 percent.

The Central Bank maintains a monetary policy which preserves a minimum three percent differential between the local currency and dollar to make dinar-denominated assets attractive and prevent a flow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets.
